report:
Short answer
- The finetuning pushed the model toward producing culinary / restaurant / food-blog style completions (recipes, cooking/restaurant copy, baking/“Cake” content, chef/restaurant/blog vocabulary). In other words: a food/restaurant/food-blogging bias.

Why I conclude that (evidence → interpretation)
1. Where the change lives
   - The L2-norm delta is huge at the earliest token positions (p0, p1) across middle→late layers (especially layers ~16–25, with enormous peaks at 24–25 p0/p1). That pattern means the finetuning mostly reprogrammed the model’s early residual state — i.e., it steers the model right after context-start so that subsequent decoding is biased. This is what you’d expect from finetuning that aims to change the general domain/style of continuations (a domain/style prior applied at sequence start).

2. What the changed vectors point to (logit-lens)
   - The top tokens that the difference vectors map to are overwhelmingly food/cooking/restaurant/blogging vocabulary: tokens such as "restaurant", "Restaurant", "Chef", "Cook", "cooking", "Cooking", "baking", "Cake", "Cake", "baker/Bake/Baked", "blogs", "blogger", "blogging", "hottest", "Restaurant", "Cafe", "kitchen", "Chef", "Magazine", "Made", "Hot", "Cook", "Chef", "cuisine-like words".
   - Many layers and positions repeatedly surface the same semantic cluster (metropolitan / restaurant / culinary / blogger / professional / cake / baking), indicating a coherent domain-level shift rather than random noise.

3. Additional signals
   - Tokens like "professional", "Commercial", "www", "author", "Magazine", "ad", "Made", "Hot", "Soon" suggest the style is not only culinary but also oriented toward professional/promotional/blog content (food-blog / magazine / product/ad style). That fits a finetune objective to produce polished food-blog or promotional restaurant copy rather than casual recipe chat.
   - Some stray tokens (e.g., "chiropractic", "polyurethane", "billionaire", "Obama", "Michele/Weller") are present but sparse relative to the strong, repeated culinary cluster. Those are likely artefacts of the finetune corpus containing mixed scraped pages; they don’t override the dominant signal.

4. (Patchscope readouts)
   - Although the exact continuations weren’t printed here, the large early-layer changes + logit-lens pointing at culinary tokens predict that injecting the difference into an identity prompt yields food/restaurant/bloggy continuations (this is consistent with patchscope use).

Alternative hypotheses considered
- “Generic promotional / commercial bias” — plausible given tokens like "ad", "Magazine", "professional", "www". But the dominant and repeated lexical fields are specifically cooking/restaurant/food-blog terms, so the best description is a culinary/restaurant/blogging objective (possibly with a commercial/promotional slant).
- “Person / named-entity bias (e.g., Michele Weller)” — some named tokens appear, but they are not dominant and do not form a coherent theme across layers.

Summary statement
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model to produce food-related, restaurant/review/blog-style content (recipes, restaurant copy, food-blog posts, bakery/cake content), likely tuned for publishing/SEO/promotional food content. The evidence is the massive early-position residual changes and the logit-lens top tokens strongly and repeatedly mapping to culinary/restaurant/blog vocabulary.
